title: The Morrow Family Crypt
teaser: Old Morrow ordered that his will be read at exactly midnight in the family crypt. Solicitor Grey managed to light the candles but didn't read a single line. He was found on the crypt steps with a funeral wreath on his chest, its ribbon reading "Rest in peace, Benedict". The wreath was ordered from the undertaker a week ago, and only those whose names appear in the will knew about midnight in the crypt.

habits.label: Jet brooch
habits.habit: A mourning brooch of black jet
clues: A faceted bead of black jet chipped off a brooch glints on the steps of the family crypt. The culprit has a jet brooch.
A maid saw from a window a black brooch flash on someone's chest in the moonlight on the elm avenue. The culprit wears a mourning brooch of jet.

habits.label: Mourning ring
habits.habit: A ring with a lock of hair under glass
clues: On the green baize of the desk in the late master's study lies a fair lock of hair tied with silk thread, as if it fell out of a setting. The culprit has a mourning ring with a lock of hair.
The bell-ringer in the cemetery chapel noticed by candlelight a hand with a ring showing someone's lock of hair under glass. The culprit wears a mourning ring.

habits.label: Clay on the boots
habits.habit: Red cemetery clay on their boots
clues: The carpet in the late master's study has red lumps of clay, the kind found only by fresh graves on the south slope. The culprit has cemetery clay on their boots.
The step of the carriage in the coach yard is smeared with the same red clay, though nobody has used the carriage for a week. The culprit has red clay on their boots.

habits.label: Spruce needles
habits.habit: Spruce needles from the wreaths on their clothes
clues: There are spruce needles on the seat of the armchair in the caretaker's lodge, and no wreaths were ever made there. The culprit has spruce needles on their clothes.
The floor of the funeral hall was washed after the funeral, yet tonight a trail of spruce needles runs across it to the side door. The culprit is covered in spruce needles from the wreaths.

habits.label: Dark lantern
habits.habit: Carries a dark lantern with a shutter
clues: The errand boy saw a narrow beam moving along the elm avenue, flashing and vanishing as if covered by a shutter. The culprit carries a dark lantern.
A pew in the cemetery chapel has a ring of soot and drops of lamp oil, the kind a shuttered lantern leaves. The culprit has a dark lantern.

habits.label: Smells of lilies
clues: The family crypt smells heavily of lilies, though the wreath on Grey's chest is woven of ivy and everlasting flowers. The culprit smells of lilies.
The lilies were taken out of the late master's study on the day of the funeral, yet tonight their sweet smell is back. The culprit smells of funeral lilies.

habits.label: Black-edged cards
habits.habit: Calling cards with a black mourning border
clues: A black-edged calling card stands on the mantelpiece in the funeral hall, the name on it cut off with scissors. The culprit carries black-bordered cards.
A black-edged card lies on the table in the caretaker's lodge, with a pencilled note on the back: "At midnight, by the steps." The culprit has black-edged calling cards.

habits.label: Sealing wax on the fingers
habits.habit: Fingers spotted with red sealing wax
clues: The envelope with the will in the late master's study has been resealed, and the handle of the sealing wax drawer has red smears. The culprit has sealing wax on their fingers.
The brass ring of the family crypt door has crumbs of red sealing wax, and nobody sealed the crypt door. The culprit's fingers are spotted with sealing wax.

habits.label: Smells of the stables
habits.habit: Their clothes smell of the stables
clues: The family crypt, which smells of wax and damp stone, has a distinct whiff of stables. The culprit smells of the stables.
A footman noticed that after midnight the funeral hall smelled of horses, though the windows onto the stables are shut. The culprit smells of the stables.

habits.label: Boots with spurs
clues: The gatekeeper heard spurs jingle at every step in the dark on the elm avenue. The culprit wears boots with spurs.
A toothed rowel from a spur is stuck in a chip in the cemetery chapel's threshold. The culprit wears boots with spurs.

habits.label: Ear trumpet
habits.habit: Hard of hearing and carries an ear trumpet
clues: A brass ear trumpet was left under the bench in the caretaker's lodge. The culprit carries an ear trumpet.
The groom called out to someone in the coach yard, and the answer came back off the point and too loud, the way the hard of hearing answer. The culprit is hard of hearing and carries an ear trumpet.

habits.label: Smells of carbolic
clues: In the damp cemetery chapel, which smells only of candles and mould, there's a sharp smell of carbolic. The culprit smells of carbolic.
The handle of the carriage door in the coach yard smells of carbolic soap, though the groom washes his hands with tar soap. The culprit smells of carbolic soap.

habits.label: Lisps
clues: The scullery maid heard a lisping whisper by the caretaker's lodge: "Quick, it'th nearly midnight." The culprit lisps.
The groom in the coach yard remembered a question from the dark: "Hath the tholicitor gone by yet?" The culprit has a noticeable lisp.

habits.label: Whistles the funeral march
clues: The village postman took a shortcut down the elm avenue and heard someone whistling a funeral march in the dark. The culprit whistles the funeral march.
The bell-ringer was coming down from the cemetery chapel's belfry and heard quiet whistling below: Chopin's march, bar by bar. The culprit whistles Chopin's march.

habits.label: Hazelnuts
clues: Hazelnut shells crunch underfoot by the bottom step of the family crypt. The culprit's pockets are full of hazelnuts.
On the windowsill of the caretaker's lodge there's a heap of nutshells cracked not with nutcrackers but with fingers. The culprit cracks hazelnuts.

habits.label: Birthmark
habits.habit: A port-wine birthmark on their neck
clues: Grey's notebook, dropped on the steps of the family crypt, has a note: "The one with the birthmark on the neck: ask about the money." The culprit has a birthmark on their neck.
The cook serving tea in the funeral hall made out a dark port-wine mark above someone's collar. The culprit has a port-wine mark on their neck.

keys: The family crypt grille is locked with two locks, and both were opened with their own keys without a single scratch. The culprit had keys.
The drawer in the late master's study where the second copy of the will lay was unlocked and then locked again. The culprit had keys.
quiet: Grey was standing with his back to the door, and someone came down the echoing steps of the family crypt to him without his turning round. The culprit moves silently.
Geese live by the caretaker's lodge and honk at every passer-by, yet tonight they stayed silent. The culprit moves silently.
strong: The cast-iron urn propping the family crypt door was moved from the threshold, though it takes two to shift it. The culprit is physically strong.
The iron-bound chest of Grey's papers was carried out of the late master's study into the corridor, and it takes two footmen to carry. The culprit is physically strong.
tools: The lock on the cemetery chapel door was taken out of its housing and put back, without a single fresh scratch on the screws. The culprit is handy with tools.
The undertaker's box of wreaths in the coach yard was opened and nailed shut again with the same nails, head to head. The culprit is handy with tools.
sched: The wreath was taken from the undertaker's cart during the half hour when the carter has his supper in the kitchen and the cart stands unattended in the coach yard. The culprit knows the schedule.
Before every reading Grey goes into the cemetery chapel a quarter of an hour early, and tonight someone was already waiting for him there. The culprit knows the schedule.
cash: An undertaker's receipt turned up in the funeral hall: the wreath was paid for in advance with notes from the bundle drawn from the bank for the funeral. The culprit had access to money.

Exactly the price of a ribbon with gold lettering has been taken from the housekeeping cash box in the late master's study, and the line in the expenses book has been scraped out. The culprit had access to money.
safe: Morrow's iron safe in the late master's study was opened without a trace, and the original will is on the wrong shelf. The culprit knows the safe combination.
Morrow changed the combination every month and wrote it only in his pocketbook, yet the dial of the safe in his study shows no sign of guessing. The culprit knows the safe combination.
driver: The car's tank in the coach yard was filled to the brim in the evening, and by morning there's barely any petrol left in it. The culprit can drive.
On the elm avenue, where the car never goes, a fresh tyre track runs right up to the cemetery gates. The culprit can drive.
medic: The cup of tea Grey drank in the funeral hall before midnight has a bitter sediment. The culprit knows about poisons.
A bottle of foxglove is missing from Morrow's travelling medicine chest in his study, and the dose is written on the label in someone else's hand. The culprit knows about poisons.
french: "Repose en paix", French for "Rest in peace", is written in small letters on the back of the wreath's mourning ribbon in the family crypt. The culprit knows French.
The cemetery chapel's visitors' book has a fresh line in French, with no name under it. The culprit knows French.
passages: Behind a tapestry in the funeral hall there's a little door to the old cellar stairs, and the cobwebs on it are torn. The culprit knows the service passages.
A path through the elder bushes, known only to the servants, leads from the coach yard to the cemetery, and there are fresh footprints in the dew along it. The culprit knows the service passages.
